summary: Iter18 — Biz-Transpay public API v1/payouts (crypto withdrawals). Backend 12/12 pytest pass. Frontend /dashboard/api shows 3 quick-start cards (Encaisser/Retirer/Suivi). /dashboard/api/docs contains new 'Retraits' sidebar group with all 5 sections, 8 payout-related error codes (PAYOUT_NOT_FOUND, INSUFFICIENT_BALANCE, WITHDRAWALS_BLOCKED, INVALID_ASSET, INVALID_DESTINATION_ADDRESS, AMOUNT_TOO_LARGE, GATEWAY_INSUFFICIENT_FUNDS, GATEWAY_UNREACHABLE), all 6 statuses (pending/processing/sent/completed/failed/canceled), 7 language code samples per section (cURL, JavaScript, Node.js, PHP, Python, Java, C#), and ZERO webhook nav/headings. Refund flow verified: after IziChange sandbox rejects (no USDT.TRC20 funds), merchant balance is restored (stayed at 50 USDT across 4+ rejected payouts, `refunded_at` timestamp set on doc).

minor.issue: Idempotency store only writes on successful path — a failing payout replayed with the same Idempotency-Key creates a brand-new attempt (still refunded correctly, but not a true idempotent replay). Not spec-blocking since merchant sees consistent error response, but worth documenting.

IziChange rejection message 'PAYOUT_INSUFFICIENT_BALANCE: solde…' contains both 'balance' and 'insufficient' so it maps to GATEWAY_INSUFFICIENT_FUNDS as expected. However `error_code` stored in DB is 'unknown' (not extracted from IziChange). Cosmetic — user-facing code is correct.

issues: Spec asked for '3 nouvelles questions sur retraits' — only 2 questions explicitly say 'retrait' ('Quels réseaux/cryptos sont supportés pour les retraits ?' and 'Que se passe-t-il si la passerelle refuse mon retrait ?'). The 3rd expected one ('Pourquoi pas de webhooks ?') exists but is generic. Not blocking.

action_items: OPTIONAL: consider adding a 3rd retrait-focused FAQ (e.g. 'Combien de temps pour un retrait ?' or 'Puis-je annuler un retrait en cours ?') to fully match the spec wording.
OPTIONAL: cache failed-idempotency responses too (or at least dedupe by Idempotency-Key so a replayed failing key returns the identical error body without hitting IziChange twice).
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is now 5420 lines — still well over the 700-line threshold. Splitting v1/payments and v1/payouts into /app/backend/routes/*.py modules would materially improve maintainability.

_reconcile_payout() refunds the merchant on newly-discovered terminal failure — the check `if not po.get('refunded_at')` prevents double-refund, good. But there is a race: if the create endpoint already refunded and set refunded_at, and _reconcile_payout runs concurrently before the DB write settles, a second refund could occur. Wrap the refund in a `find_one_and_update` with `refunded_at: {$exists: false}` filter for atomicity.
list endpoint fires up to 10 upstream reconcile tasks per request without dedup — same concern as v1/payments list. A merchant paginating heavily will hammer IziChange.

success_rate.frontend: 100% (all spec items validated except minor FAQ count)

seed_data_creation: Seeded merchant balance_usdt=50 (idempotent — pre-existing account). Created ~5 sk_test_ keys named TEST_iter18_* via /api/merchant/keys. Created ~4 failed merchant_payouts docs (all refunded).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Payload for POST /api/v1/payouts uses field `network` (string, not `accepted_networks` — that is only for v1/payments PAY-IN). Valid test TRC20 address: TJRabPrwbZy45sbavfcjinPJC18kjpRTv8. IziChange sandbox has no USDT.TRC20 liquidity, so every real payout attempt returns GATEWAY_INSUFFICIENT_FUNDS via error message classification — expected behavior. Idempotency store is only populated on success responses in current implementation. To seed merchant balance: `python3 -c "import asyncio,os; from motor.motor_asyncio import AsyncIOMotorClient; asyncio.run(AsyncIOMotorClient(os.environ['MONGO_URL'])['<DB>'].users.update_one({'email':'bizboy966@gmail.com'},{'\$set':{'balance_usdt':50}}))"` — after sourcing /app/backend/.env.
